identity.title: LLM-SRBench: A New Benchmark for Scientific Equation Discovery with Large Language Models

problem.claim: Assess whether LLM-based methods can discover scientific equations from challenging problems.

gap.claim: Existing benchmarks often use common equations vulnerable to LLM memorization, inflating performance measures that may not reflect actual discovery.

contributions.claim: Introduces LLM-SRBench, a benchmark of 239 problems spanning four scientific domains, designed to reduce trivial memorization.
Defines LSR-Transform for uncommon mathematical representations of common physical models and LSR-Synth for synthetic, discovery-driven problems requiring data-driven reasoning.
Reports an evaluation of several state-of-the-art methods using both open and closed LLMs.

stated_novelty.claim: The benchmark combines transformed and synthetic equation-discovery problems specifically intended to test reasoning beyond memorization.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Authors report that the best-performing evaluated system achieves only 31.5% symbolic accuracy on LLM-SRBench.
Authors report evaluating several state-of-the-art methods with both open and closed LLMs.

narrative_sequence.summary: Scientific equation discovery supports deriving laws governing natural phenomena, and LLMs are being considered for hypothesis generation.
Common-equation benchmarks can permit memorization and produce inflated measures of discovery capability.
LLM-SRBench addresses this concern with 239 problems across four domains, organized into transformed-model and synthetic discovery categories.
Evaluation across open and closed LLMs yields a reported best symbolic accuracy of 31.5%.

source_observation.claim: The benchmark separates transformed versions of familiar models from synthetic problems to distinguish reasoning beyond memorization from data-driven discovery.

lessons.interpretation: Separating challenge types can make a benchmark’s intended capability dimensions more inspectable.
lessons.application: When introducing an evaluation resource, define task categories that isolate competing explanations for success, such as memorization versus reasoning.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when the target capability cannot be cleanly decomposed or when category construction changes the task substantially.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the four scientific domains, evaluated method names, or the benchmark’s data and scoring protocol.
The reported 31.5% symbolic accuracy lacks confidence intervals, per-category results, and comparison details.
